name: Drekk ChemWall Acid-Environment Full Suit
description:
Matte black with high-visibility acid-yellow chevrons across the shoulders and thighs, the ChemWall is a one-piece chemical barrier suit made from Drekk's proprietary ViperSkin — a chlorosulfonated polyethylene outer shell bonded to a closed-cell foam thermal liner. Designed for Shelf acid-rain zones and Circuit-level industrial cleaning crews. The silhouette is bulky, utilitarian, and carries no pretense.

The integrated hood is sealed with a bayonet-lock visor ring accepting standard 40mm filter canisters. Taped seams run in bright yellow contrast stitching for visual inspection. Integrated tail-exit gusset at rear seam for gene-compatible wearers.
functionality: Resists pH 0–2 acid splash and prolonged acid-rain exposure; bayonet-lock visor accepts standard industrial filter canisters; rear gusset accommodates tail geneware without compromising the chemical seal; integrated over-boot sole rated for caustic floor spills.
what_it_says: You go into places that eat through anything cheaper.
story_hooks: A cleaning crew member finds a sealed document packet fused inside a corroded drainage pipe — still legible, and someone very powerful wants it back.
The ViperSkin compound has a known failure mode at temperatures above 60°C; a batch was shipped to Shelf workers without the recall notice.
A gene-compatible worker with a prehensile tail used the rear gusset to smuggle out biosamples from a restricted chemical site — and now needs help disappearing.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist one-piece silhouette with pronounced shoulder and thigh bulk. The matte black creates a void-like presence broken only by acid-yellow chevron warning stripes and high-visibility seam stitching. The integrated hood reads as an extension of the torso rather than a separate element. Overall impression: industrial hazmat worker crossed with deep-dive salvage operator.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed and intentionally oversized through the torso and limbs to accommodate layering and movement in contaminated zones. Compression at wrists, ankles, and neck seal points. The rear gusset allows for augmented spinal hardware or tail modifications without compromising the seal.
physical_description.primary_material: ViperSkin — proprietary chlorosulfonated polyethylene outer shell (chemical-resistant, acid-neutral pH-reactive) bonded to closed-cell foam thermal liner (inherent insulation, buoyancy in liquid exposure)
physical_description.texture: Outer shell is matte and slightly slick, designed to shed liquid chemicals without absorption. Seams are raised and tactilely distinct due to yellow contrast stitching. The thermal liner is cushioned and slightly compressible, visible at neck and cuff edges.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte black field with acid-yellow chevrons on shoulders and outer thighs, yellow taped seams throughout for structural and regulatory visibility
physical_description.closures: Integrated hood with bayonet-lock visor ring (40mm filter canister compatible). Body sealed via continuous taped seams. Magnetic snap wrist and ankle cuffs for rapid removal in emergency decontamination.
distinctive_features: Bayonet-lock integrated hood with 40mm filter canister port
High-visibility yellow chevron warning stripes (regulatory requirement for Shelf-zone work)
Contrast-stitched taped seams (yellow) for visual integrity inspection
Closed-cell foam thermal liner (visible at collar/cuff)
Matte finish to prevent light-reflection in hazardous chemical environments
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4-5 functional. Affordable working-class equipment with zero luxury markers. Drekk Heavy Fabrication is a mid-tier industrial supplier, not haute couture.
physical_description.cultural_context: Signals hazmat technician, Circuit-level industrial crew, Shelf-zone salvager, or sub-grade chemical processing worker. Wearing this outside contamination zones reads as either off-shift exhaustion or deliberate anti-corporate posturing.
physical_description.condition_typical: Weathered and patched. Outer shell shows acid-etch marks, scuffed matte finish, and discolored seam tape from repeated exposure. Thermal liner compressed and slightly torn at high-friction zones. Still functional and seal-rated, but visibly lived-in.
